hero.title: Vibecoding: AI Writes Your Code
hero.subtitle: When you tell AI what you want — and it writes the code.

lead.paragraph1: In 2025, Andrej Karpathy invented a new word: vibecoding. Karpathy is an AI researcher. Vibecoding means: You tell the AI what you want. The AI writes the code for you.
lead.paragraph2: Before, a program took two hours. Now: ten minutes describing, then 30 minutes checking. But be careful: There are three dangerous traps.

paradigm.title: The Big Change
paradigm.analogy: Imagine an architect. Before, he built every wall himself. Now he has workers (the AI). He makes the blueprint (prompt). The workers build from it. The architect checks the work.
paradigm.scientific: Vibecoding means: You write in normal language what the program should do. The AI turns it into real code. This is the newest step: From machine code to normal language.
paradigm.analogyBreak: But: Real workers learn and improve. AI forgets everything after each session. And: Checking a building is easy. Checking code is hard.
paradigm.roleShift: Your job changes: You don't write code anymore. You check code. You tell the AI what to change. It is like a conversation.
paradigm.eightTwenty: The AI does about 80 percent of the work. You do the important 20 percent: The planning. The tricky edge cases. The security.

tools.title: The Tools
tools.intro: There are different AI tools. Some help a little. Others do almost everything alone. You choose how much the AI should do.

completion.label: Suggests lines
completion.description: Suggests single lines. Like a GPS in your car.

editor.label: Editor that knows the project
editor.description: Changes many files at once. Like a co-driver reading the map.

supervised.label: Agent with supervision
supervised.description: Plans and works on its own. You watch. Like a driving student.

autonomous.label: Agent without supervision
autonomous.description: Does everything alone. You just say the goal. Like a taxi.

literacy.title: Important: Read More, Write Less
literacy.text: Vibecoding has a surprise: You write less code. But you must read more code. Understanding AI code is harder than understanding your own code.
literacy.insight: Reading becomes more important than writing. If you don't check AI code, you get problems later.

risks.title: The Dangers
risks.intro: Vibecoding has three big dangers. Also: The AI likes to build security holes.

hallucination.title: 1. Wrong Code:
hallucination.text: The code starts. But it has hidden errors. The AI misses special cases.

contextLoss.title: 2. Forgetting:
contextLoss.text: In big projects, the AI forgets rules. It makes errors that were already fixed.

cargoCult.title: 3. Blind Accepting:
cargoCult.text: If you take code you don't understand: Later nobody can fix it.

failScenario.title: Example: Everything Goes Wrong
failScenario.text: A beginner builds a chatbot. On his computer everything works. On the internet: Passwords visible. Huge costs. Crashes.
failScenario.consequences: Everything worked — until real users came.

risks.bottomLine: Experienced developers use vibecoding best. They know what good code looks like.

obsolete.title: Wrong: Programmers Are Not Needed Anymore
obsolete.text: Wrong. Programmers now check the code. Without knowledge you cannot find errors.

autonomy.title: Wrong: The Most Independent Tool Is Always Best
autonomy.text: Wrong. For important code (security, money) you need more control. Choose the right tool for the job.

safe.title: Wrong: If the Code Runs, Everything Is Safe
safe.text: Wrong. AI code often runs. But it has hidden problems. Checking is a must.

takeaways.title: Key Points
takeaways.point1: Vibecoding: You say WHAT. The AI does HOW.
takeaways.point2: Your new job: Check code instead of write code.
takeaways.point3: There are four levels: From suggestions to full automation. Choose wisely.
takeaways.point4: Three dangers: Wrong code, forgetting, blind accepting. Always check!

q1.question: What is vibecoding?
q1.b: You tell the AI what you want. It writes the code.
q1.explanation: Vibecoding means: You describe in normal language. The AI writes the code.

q2.question: Your program needs a secure login. Which tool fits best?
q2.a: The most independent tool — finished quickly
q2.b: A simple tool with lots of your own control — security is important
q2.d: A medium tool — the AI does most of it
q2.explanation: For security code you need more control. A simple tool is safer.

q3.question: The AI builds a login. It works. But passwords are not encrypted. What problem is this?
q3.b: The programmer did not understand the code
q3.c: Wrong code — looks good but has an error
q3.d: The tool was set up wrong
q3.explanation: This is wrong code: It runs but has a dangerous error.

q4.question: A beginner says: I don't need to learn to read code. The AI writes everything. What is wrong?
q4.b: You must be able to check AI code — for that you must be able to read
q4.d: Only experts need to read code
q4.explanation: You write less code. But you must read more code and check it.

q5.question: What are the important 20 percent that humans must do?
q5.b: Planning, special cases, security, and checking
q5.explanation: The important 20 percent: Planning, special cases, security. That is where the value is.

q6.question: A team builds an app with vibecoding. After six months nobody understands the code. What is the problem?
q6.b: Vibecoding debt: The team accepted code it does not understand
q6.explanation: When nobody understands the code, nobody can fix errors. That is vibecoding debt.

checkpoint.title: Did You Understand?
checkpoint.q1: Why do programmers now check code instead of writing it?
checkpoint.q2: Which of the four levels is best for important code?
checkpoint.q3: What are the three dangers of vibecoding?

enrichment.intro: Put together a vibe-coding prompt from building blocks. Pick a role, tech stack, task, and quality rules. Watch a clear prompt take shape.
enrichment.instruction: Click one block in each group. Your prompt appears below.

hint.title: Why a builder?
hint.description: Good prompts always have 4 parts: the role, the tech stack, the task, and the quality. The builder shows these 4 parts. And you see at once when a part is missing.

vc_r1.label: Senior Developer
vc_r1.text: You are a senior developer. You write clean code that is easy to maintain.

vc_r2.label: Software Architect
vc_r2.text: You are a software architect. Explain your design choices. Suggest alternatives.

vc_r3.label: Pair Programmer
vc_r3.text: You are my pair programmer. Think out loud. Ask questions. Explain your decisions.

vc_e1.label: React + TypeScript
vc_e1.text: The project uses React and TypeScript. It also uses Tailwind CSS and Vite.

vc_e2.label: Python + FastAPI
vc_e2.text: The project is a backend in Python. It uses FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, and PostgreSQL.

vc_e3.label: Angular + Optimus UI
vc_e3.text: The project uses Angular with Optimus UI components. Signals manage the state.

vc_t1.label: Build Feature
vc_t1.text: Build this feature completely. Create all needed files. Update existing ones.

vc_t2.label: Fix Bug
vc_t2.text: Find and fix this bug. Explain the root cause. Explain why your fix works.

vc_t3.label: Refactoring
vc_t3.text: Refactor the code for better readability. Keep the same behavior.

vc_f1.label: With Tests
vc_f1.text: Write a unit test for every new function. Use the test framework the project already has.

vc_f2.label: Explain Steps
vc_f2.text: Explain each step. Briefly say why you made each design choice.

vc_f3.label: Clean Code
vc_f3.text: Follow clean code rules: clear names, small functions, no magic numbers.
